q: In the Roman calendar, on what date did the Ides of March fall?
note: Caesar was assassinated on it in 44 BC, which is why Shakespeare has a soothsayer warn him to beware it.

q: Which NASA mission carried the first humans to land on the Moon in July 1969?
note: Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit while his two crewmates walked on the surface.

q: Whose almost untouched tomb did the archaeologist Howard Carter open in the Valley of the Kings in 1922?
note: He was a minor pharaoh in life; the intact tomb is what made him famous.

q: What name is given to the flowering of art and learning that began in Italy in the 14th century and spread across Europe?
note: The word simply means "rebirth" in French.

q: Which US state spent almost ten years as an independent republic before joining the Union in 1845?
note: It broke from Mexico in 1836 and ran its own government, currency and foreign policy for nine years.

q: What name is given to the network of ancient trade routes that carried goods between China and the Mediterranean world?
note: The name was coined in the 19th century, long after the routes were in use.

q: Who made the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic in 1927?
note: He flew New York to Paris in about 33 hours in the Spirit of St. Louis, staying awake the whole way.

q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, honoured in 1903 for work on radioactivity?
note: She later won a second Nobel, in chemistry, in 1911.

q: Which Paris fortress and prison was stormed by a crowd on 14 July 1789?
note: Only seven prisoners were being held inside at the time.

q: Which is older: Harvard University, or Isaac Newton?
note: Harvard was founded in 1636; Newton was born six years later, at the end of 1642.

q: Which came first: the founding of the Nintendo company, or the end of the Ottoman Empire?
note: Nintendo started out making playing cards in 1889; the Ottoman sultanate was abolished in 1922.

q: Which European settlement in what is now the United States was founded first: St. Augustine in Florida, or Jamestown in Virginia?
note: The Spanish founded St. Augustine in 1565, forty-two years before the English reached Jamestown in 1607.

q: Which is older: Westminster Abbey in London, or the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan?
note: The abbey church was consecrated in 1065; Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.

q: Which came first: the first Olympic Games of ancient Greece, or the founding of the Roman Republic?
note: The games are traditionally dated to 776 BC, the republic to 509 BC.

q: Which came first: the Hijra, Muhammad's migration to Medina, or the Viking raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne?
note: The Hijra took place in 622; Lindisfarne was raided in 793.

q: Anne Frank was born in the same year as which American civil rights leader?
note: Both were born in 1929, he in January and she in June.

q: Which Russian ruler was the first to be crowned Tsar of All Russia, in 1547?
note: He was a near contemporary of Elizabeth I, and the two exchanged letters.

q: Which country became, in 1893, the first self-governing nation to give women the vote in national elections?
note: A petition with nearly 32,000 signatures helped push the bill through.

q: Which Spanish conquistador led the expedition that overthrew the Inca Empire in the 1530s?
note: He founded Lima in 1535 as the capital of Spanish Peru.

q: Which English mathematician led the wartime work on breaking the German Enigma cipher at Bletchley Park?
note: His pre-war paper on computable numbers laid groundwork for the modern computer.

q: What name is given to the operation that supplied West Berlin by air for nearly a year in 1948 and 1949?
note: At its peak, aircraft were landing in the city every few minutes around the clock.

q: Which Japanese period began in 1868 with the restoration of direct imperial rule and a rush to modernise?
note: Within forty years Japan had railways, a modern navy and a written constitution.

q: Which Egyptian queen ruled as pharaoh in her own right and built a terraced temple at Deir el-Bahari?
note: She reigned for about twenty years in the 15th century BC and was often depicted as a male king.

q: Which German airship caught fire while landing at Lakehurst, New Jersey, in May 1937?
note: The disaster effectively ended the brief era of passenger airship travel.

q: Which US president served the shortest term, dying just 31 days after his inauguration in 1841?
note: His grandson Benjamin Harrison later served a full term as president.

q: Which Habsburg ruler was both Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain before abdicating his crowns in 1556?
note: He split his inheritance, leaving Spain to his son Philip II and the imperial title to his brother Ferdinand.

q: Which ruler founded the Mughal Empire after winning the first Battle of Panipat in 1526?
note: He claimed descent from both Timur and Genghis Khan.

q: Which African country defeated an invading Italian army at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, keeping its independence?
note: Emperor Menelik II's victory forced Italy to recognise Ethiopian independence by treaty that same year.

q: Which Southeast Asian empire was ruled from the temple city of Angkor?
note: Angkor Wat, its most famous temple, was built in the 12th century under Suryavarman II.

q: Which came first: the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza, or the death of the last known woolly mammoths?
note: The pyramid went up around 2560 BC, while a small mammoth population survived on Arctic Wrangel Island until roughly 2000 BC.
